steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I thought you'd have gotten everyone to help fix up the guts of this tower by now.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: And I thought you'd be getting ready for the Speaker's speech, Vina. I'd rather not meddle with the designers while they work anyway.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: They know how to build a museum better than I do, and I'm looking forward to what little surprises the 'Knights of the Tower Museum' they're making has in store for me.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: But carving a monument commemorating the Knights? That's something I've got to do myself.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Here, have a look. How is it?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Never took you for a sculptor.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Master Mitchell taught me how when I was really young. Though he'd always get so drunk he'd forget to teach me his special techniques.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Come on over and I'll introduce you. This is Master Finn, the last Captain of the Watch, and the elder knight I was closest to.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: This is Old Ferguson, the one who taught me to drink. This is Master Bailey, who did her best to teach me how to do makeup.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: And here's Master Mitchell—not my carving, though. He made it himself after a night at the pub.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: This is Carl, the crybaby. This is Martin. Every week he'd sneak off before getting sent back by his family. This is Karen...

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: And then there's... There's...
Vina gently hugs Dagda, comforting her.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Thanks, Vina, but I'm fine.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: It's just that every time I come back here, those fading memories of mine become a lot clearer.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: You carved your own name too. 'Isabelle Montague'...

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: The Knights of the Tower never left. We're still here. Master Finn would be glad to hear it.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: You know, Parliament could retain the institution of the Knights, even if you—

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Our duty is already over, no?

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Victoria has no need for a monarch, so naturally she has no need for the Knights. Let the past be remembered in a museum. That's the best ending we could ask for.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Since there's no more need to light up the tower for the palace's sake, my own duty's done as well.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: These days, Londinium is no longer home to Isabelle, the Knight of the Tower. There's just Dagda now. Dagda of the Glasgow Gang.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: But Vina, if you still have need of the Knights, I won't hesitate. Just say the word.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Oh, don't tease me, Dagda. You heard those rumors too?

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: We've been looking into who's been spreading them. But it seems there's a lot of people who believe, even wholeheartedly support the idea that—

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: 'Vina Victoria will be crowned King.'

steps.name: Sulking Child
steps.text: Eliseo! Eliseo! Please wait!

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Oh, Jenna. More questions you'd like to ask me?

steps.name: Sulking Child
steps.text: Miss Molly wants to invite you to stay and watch us rehearse our new play—

steps.name: Sulking Child
steps.text: Also, Eliseo, could you help me prove something?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Sulking Child
steps.text: Jamie and I had a wager. That even if my gran and I moved to Columbia, we wouldn't be much better off than we are now.

steps.name: Sulking Child
steps.text: His dad said that in Columbia, kids like us wouldn't get to go to school, and there wouldn't be any teachers who'd want to teach us how to do plays...

steps.name: Sulking Child
steps.text: Jamie said everything you told us in class was a lie.
Jenna, you should be up on stage for the rehearsal. Don't be bothering Eliseo now.

steps.name: Sulking Child
steps.text: Ah! M—Miss Molly!

steps.name: Sulking Child
steps.text: I was just inviting him to stay and watch...

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Allow me. Jamie's waiting for you on stage. He's about to cry any moment now.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Without you, he can't say any of his lines. Go on.

steps.name: Sulking Child
steps.text: Oh, he's so annoying... Alright, I'll go...

steps.name: Sulking Child
steps.text: You've got to stay and watch, Eliseo!

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: *sigh* Do forgive the children, Eliseo. They tend to just speak their mind.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: I must admit, I'm not too familiar with Columbia, and I'm not entirely sure how Infected children would be treated—

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: They'd be treated very well!

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: ...So long as their guardians can afford health insurance.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: I see.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: The children are very fond of you, and I'm grateful that you took the time to explain how they should take care of themselves after infection. It's important for them to know.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Thank you, truly.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: I have to give the same lectures to kids back home pretty often, so it's no trouble at all. Honestly, I'd like to thank you for letting me teach them.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: I thought since Parliament's on bad terms with Pure Heart Medical, the schools wouldn't let me near the children.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Parliament's never forbidden us from reaching out to you though? On the contrary, they tend to approve of this sort of thing as long as we're quiet about it, up to a certain degree.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Not just you, either. We've also invited Rhodes Island's doctors over to give the children checkups and lessons.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Parliament knows that children will need assistance.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: But there's only so much that checkups and lessons can do for them. What they need is medicine and treatment.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: I know. But all we can do now is stay by their side and make sure they are not overcome by fear.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: At least at this school, they can still live like how they used to... Like regular people.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: I really admire you, Molly.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Back home, if a young Infected is as energetic as these kids here, it usually means their family is pretty well-off.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: But here... I hear some kids had nowhere to go, so you gave them shelter at the school. You've got them putting on plays, ones that bring hope to the people here.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: That's amazing.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: You flatter me, Eliseo.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: I am merely following in the footsteps of those teachers who can no longer return to school... Especially the lady I respect the most.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Do you mean Lady Golding? I heard Heidi mention her before.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Yes. The play we are rehearsing today was the last she ever wrote in this classroom.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: It's a lovely little tale. Two young children go on many adventures to find a fowlbeast that can chase away any illness, which saves their sickly friend.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Lady Heidi once asked me if Lady Golding ever called it a 'meaningless consolation' when she was writing it...

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: But why?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Is it alright if I stay and watch them rehearse, Molly?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: For the sake of the children, and so I can show how much I respect you, and your lady.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: I have a feeling that maybe here, in Londinium, there's still a lot I can do to help.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: ...For Lady Golding.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: ...For Lady Golding.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Are all the MPs present?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: They are.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: How much longer until the city-wide broadcast?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Two minutes.

a.text: It was an evening close to New Year's.

After several long years living in fear, most folk could finally feel at ease and enjoy dinner with their families, listening to the Speaker of Parliament's broadcast together. They even started calling it the 'Dinnertime Declaration' in jest.
Pity that dinner didn't taste so good.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Testing, testing, *cough*—

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Shall I begin?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Go ahead.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: This is Vina Victoria. As Speaker of Londinium's Parliament, I now address all the city's residents who took part in resistance during the war, and who yet live.

steps.name: Vina's Voice
steps.text: Two months ago, we walked out from the midst of tragedy.

steps.name: Stressed Soldier
steps.text: You lot shut up! Can't you tell the Speaker's started her speech already?

steps.name: Vina's Voice
steps.text: On behalf of Parliament, allow me to convey our respect to those heroes who contributed to the war effort.

steps.name: Vina's Voice
steps.text: Every citizen, every soldier of the ducal alliance, every fighter of the Exemplars.

steps.name: Vina's Voice
steps.text: The city will remember each and every one of your deeds, and honor all those who are no longer with us.
The pub falls silent as everyone lifts their cups.

steps.name: Stressed Soldier
steps.text: To you, my brothers... and to me.

steps.name: Vina's Voice
steps.text: Now, Londinium has begun her long road to recovery. Order will be reestablished, and those lives once so familiar to us will return.

steps.name: Vina's Voice
steps.text: But that's not all. In regards to the Exemplars, those glorious fighters of extraordinary circumstance, Parliament has decided to reserve this unit designation forevermore, so that we may commemorate both the past and the present of these troops.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: I can hear the children singing, and the retired soldiers singing alongside them. Seems like they're in a good mood.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: The song they're singing is from the end of the play.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: The sickly child finally recovers, and together, they find happiness.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: I... expected those homeless soldiers to care a lot more about the Speaker's speech.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Of course they care, but they are of firm belief that the Speaker will not abandon them.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: After all the suffering endured, happiness will surely come, Eliseo. Do you believe so?

steps.name: Vina's Voice
steps.text: The Exemplars came together once more for one simple dream: to go home. No matter their status, no matter their standing.

steps.name: Vina's Voice
steps.text: Now, this dream of theirs has become reality. We are home now. We have reached the end of the road.

steps.name: Disdainful Mercenary
steps.text: Hah, 'reached the end of the road'.

steps.name: Disdainful Mercenary
steps.text: Seems this Speaker lady really is set on disbanding them. What an idiot, pulling apart your army of mates—

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Then what do you propose she should do with such a motley crew?

spans.text: propose she should do with such a motley crew?

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Keep chasing those Sarkaz for the kill? Or set their sights on the dukes?

steps.name: Disdainful Mercenary
steps.text: Uh...

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: We've got better things to worry about than the Exemplars.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Such as replenishing our strength as quickly as we can. Focus on that instead.

steps.name: Vina's Voice
steps.text: Many former Exemplars have joined the Defense Force's ranks, continuing to protect our homeland.

steps.name: Vina's Voice
steps.text: As for those who no longer wish to bear arms, they have the right to enjoy peace alongside their families.

steps.name: Vina's Voice
steps.text: Parliament promises each and every one of our Exemplar comrades a place to settle down. It may take a long time for this to come to fruition, but the door to the Speaker's office is forever open to my friends—

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: I'm afraid it'll take a few years to see this through. You've got a long road ahead of you, Vina.

steps.name: Happy Worker
steps.text: Coming along for dinner, Catherine? There's a fair few old retired blokes who've reported back to the factory.

steps.name: Happy Worker
steps.text: They'll be real happy to see you!

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Sure you're not just angling for my stash of smokes? I worked real hard to collect them.

steps.name: Happy Worker
steps.text: Hehe.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Fine, fine, I'll come along. Oh, right. While you're at it, tell everyone to bring a few friends along.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Once Parliament helps us restart more factories, the hands we have now won't be enough.

steps.name: Vina's Voice
steps.text: And I, Vina Victoria, do promise to every one of this city's residents, that in this coming future without a king—
The broadcast abruptly comes to an end. As it does so, Dagda hears an uproar suddenly echo through the skies above the city.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Why the cut-off? What's... What's going on at Parliament?

steps.name: Nervous Worker
steps.text: Madam Speaker, Madam Delphine, while I was fixing up the broadcast system, I noticed this old component.

steps.name: Nervous Worker
steps.text: It's ancient scrap, should've been replaced when His Majesty Alistair was on the throne.

steps.name: Nervous Worker
steps.text: Who would've thought an unremarkable thing like this could still hold up until now! My mentor never told me anything about this!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: So it's all just an accident?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Why was there suddenly something on your maintenance checklist that wasn't there before?

steps.name: Nervous Worker
steps.text: Iؙ—I just followed what the system synced up to me—
Ladies and gentlemen, may I sit in on this round of parliamentary discussion?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Earl of March.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Eleanor. My name's not hard to remember, Vina.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: You seem rather surprised to see me here. What, did no one tell you?

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: It seems your informants have been lax of late, Lady Delphine.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Londinium has no need for... 'informants' to host a guest, my Lady. The city welcomes every Victorian who loves this land.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Lovely to hear.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Then I suppose you won't mind if I invite a few dukes to revisit an old haunt for a little reunion.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Judging by the time, they should be arriving any moment now. Considering their sensitive position, the dukes are hesitant to drop in on any specific person's home, so I was forced to borrow one of your places.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: I hope Parliament will understand. You're also welcome to join in, Vina. And you too of course, Delphine.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: I know you are about to leave for Windermere. There are a few old friends who hope you could take their condolences for your mother along with you.
Eleanor doffs her hat, greeting Delphine with a smile.
She then immediately walks to Vina's side and lowers her voice.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: I loved your speech, a very sensible decision. Yet...

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Far, far too impatient. There are some things you are free to say to us, but not to the common public.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: This is for their own good, and yours too.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: So you were the one who cut our signal.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: We'll be assembling at the Royal Academy of Sciences, Vina. It won't take too long, so don't be late.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: By the by, sometimes, there's no need for you to think you haven't done enough. The changes this city has seen are far beyond what I imagined.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: I assumed Your Grace would have less of an appetite.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: I've always been a practical lad, Eleanor.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: We all know the situation in Londinium. This light wine and bread is already enough to show us the Speaker's good faith.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: The Duke of Wellington is absent, yet again.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: *sigh* It seems the alliance between yourself and His Grace is not as reliable as we imagined.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: We all know we're here for more than just pleasantries, Your Grace. Old Wellington would never have come in the first place.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: How do you believe we should treat with Duke of Wellington, Vina?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: If it has naught to do with Londinium, it has naught to do with me.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Oh, really?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Would he really care what you all think? He's always been one to seize the initiative.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: All I know is that since the battle for the walls ended two months ago, the engines of the Gastrell and the other frigates have not rested for even a moment.

spans.text: All I know is that since the battle for the walls ended two months ago, the engines of the
and the other frigates have not rested for even a moment.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Wellington has been waiting for you to bite, and I'm afraid to say that he's very disappointed in you all.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Quite right.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: But what you see is merely one side of the matter, Delphine Windermere.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: In Old Wellington's eyes, it is still far far too early to decide what sort of relationship will exist between Tara and Victoria.

spans.text: In Old Wellington's eyes, it is still far
too early to decide what sort of relationship will exist between Tara and Victoria.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: In these two months, we have had a... tacit understanding. So long as nobody moves to break the silence, then silence we shall enjoy.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: But really, it's Her Grace over here whose emissaries are always sneaking into Wellington's demesne. She's much better qualified than I to speak on the matter, no?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Once I return, I will be investigating who has been going against my orders.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: After you return to Windermere, young Delphine, I would happily welcome some tired guests at the Lynncardine winery, whenever you like—

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Could we dispense with the banalities already?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Londinium may welcome all Victorians, but we have no time to waste chatting with each and every one of them. There are still many issues affecting our citizens that need urgent handling, all more important than the people sitting here.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I am, of course, well aware that your sudden visit to Londinium is also thanks to an... ahem, tacit understanding.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I know that Wellington's only an excuse. Parliament will not interfere in this matter. So if what you're going to discuss next doesn't involve Parliament, then I don't need to waste my time here—

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: That's where you're wrong, Vina. The Duke of Wellington's choice really does have something to do with you. Or to be more precise, it's to do with the late king. Your late father.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Twenty-six years ago, Old Wellington never cast a vote in the matter of how to handle your father. He simply watched in silence as King Alistair was led from the throne to the gallows...

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Thereafter, he was disappointed. Disappointed in Victoria. Disappointed in the dukes. Disappointed in your father.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: From that moment on, the tug of Tara's undercurrent has never ceased.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Duke Windermere never mentioned any of this to me—

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Your mother didn't care. No one regretted executing the King. Sorry, Vina, you know I don't mean anything untoward.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Just because Old Wellington himself will never come to Londinium doesn't mean that he has no interest in the city, or in you.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: For the time being, we still do not know his true intentions. But just because the throne has sat idle for many years does not mean Victoria needs no king.
Vina does not understand where Eleanor is going with this. She already made clear her refusal long ago.
The kingship, the crown. They were never what she needed—

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Bloody hell, Vina, patrol's just come by your office to tell you—

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: The crown's been stolen from the throne room!

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Pardon?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: It seems our meeting must be postponed, Speaker Victoria. There are side matters that require your attention.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: If you need help, Vina, you know where to find me.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Chances are we'll be troubling you a little longer, Madam Speaker.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: You sodding—
